findings.title: audible join: fm_slow_listen.mp3 + van.mp3 + van.mp3
findings.detail: The prompt voice sounds American (rhotic 'word') while the target words sound British. The components are audibly separate recordings with differing acoustic profiles and pitch/tone. (judge 4/10; heard: ˈlɪsən tə maɪ sloʊ wɜːrd ... v-æ-n ... væn)

findings.title: audible join: t_and_sometimes.mp3 + dh.mp3
findings.detail: The transition and acoustic match between the prompt and sound are seamless, but the sound pronounced is clearly /v/ rather than the expected voiced /ð/. (judge 6/10; heard: ənd ˈsʌmtaɪmz v)

findings.title: audible join: listen.mp3 + cloth.mp3
findings.detail: 'cloth' is noticeably punchier and louder than 'Listen', making it sound pasted in. Additionally, the final consonant uses th-fronting ([f] instead of [θ]), which is non-standard for synthetic phonics instruction. (judge 6/10; heard: lɪsən klɒf)
